text:
maria: Quick sync — I want to run a low-overhead profiling pass against the prod-like GPU pool to surface kernel hotspots and KV-cache latency interactions. Goal: keep tracing overhead <= 1.5% on p95 tail latency. Sampling vs short full traces? Tradeoffs:

simon: For this use-case I vote for burst full traces + continuous light sampling. Example plan: 10s full nsys traces every 2 minutes on 3 hosts (rotated) + perfetto heap/cpu sampling at 100ms on one host. That gives high-fidelity windows without continuous heavy impact. :thumbsup:

lee: Agree with rotational full traces. Two extra notes: 1) run at steady QPS (dont ramp during trace) so batcher behavior is stable; 2) pin model & kernel selection flags so we don't mix kernel variants. Also we should sample across at least 3 batch sizes (1, 8, 32).

ashley: For KV cache effects we should inject a synthetic prefix mix to hit >80% cache pressure during one of the full traces — otherwise hotspots hiding under cold-cache behavior. I can add a small harness to the test runner.

maria: Good call. Proposed guardrails for the run: abort if p50 increases >5ms or p95 increases >10ms vs baseline, or if throughput drops >3%. ops-bot, can we enforce automatic cancel on those triggers?

ops-bot: @maria scheduled job will monitor metrics. Auto-cancel rule added: trace.cancel if (trace.overhead.p95_pct > 1.5) OR (throughput_drop_pct > 3) OR (latency_p95_delta_ms > 10).

simon: Example nsys invocation for the short full traces (we'll template and run via Ansible):
```bash
nsys profile -o /tmp/trace_$HOST_$ITER -t cuda,nvtx,osrt --duration=10 
  --sample=cpu --trace-fork=1 --force-overwrite 
  --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi:start,end
```
Notes: use capture-range to avoid startup noise, duration=10s, rotate hosts, and keep iteration ids.

lee: For perfetto/continuous sampling keep interval coarse (100-200ms) and only capture kernel timelines + thread states. We don't need full GPU timelines continuously.

ashley: When analyzing, focus on: kernel occ/inst ratio, memcpy vs kernel time, and KV-cache lookups per token. If memcpy spikes during certain batch sizes that points to wrong kernel/batching choice.

maria: Analysis plan: run traces -> generate flamegraphs (nsys report & perfetto UI) -> tag top-3 kernel suspects -> run microbench kernel-only reproducer to verify regression. If reproducer confirms, create a rollout block.

perf-bot: Reminder: add metric trace.overhead.p95_pct to Console (category: infra.profiling). Also add a per-host trace_count tag.

maria: One outstanding question: sampling frequency vs overhead. If we sample CPU every 100ms we see good thread-switch info but overhead creeps. I'd rather default to 250ms for long-run perfetto sampling and keep the 10s full traces for fidelity. Any objections?

simon: 250ms sounds safe for continuous. Full traces will catch short-lived kernel interactions. Also consider enabling per-kernel counters (SMUtil, L2 hit) on a subset of runs. That adds noise but only in canary runs.

lee: Also document exact burn-in window (first 30s excluded) and which metrics count as baseline. We should keep reproducibility so we can compare across dates.

maria: OK — plan: schedule canary tomorrow 09:00 PT on the dedicated perf pool. Rotate 3 hosts, batch sizes [1,8,32], KV-pressure scenario on host #2. Ops will auto-cancel on guardrails. I'll post the job id here once queued. Thanks everyone. :rocket:

ashley: I'll prepare the KV pressure harness and the reproducer targets.

simon: I'll template the nsys/perfetto job and verification checklist.

maria: If anyone has additional small checks (e.g., GPU power cap toggles, cuBLAS env vars) add them to the run doc in the repo. We want to avoid noisy confounders.

lee: SGTM.
